transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-08
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dana Lee (Celestis Head of Search), Marco Ruiz (Celestis ML Eng), Emily Chen (Celestis Platform Eng)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Discussed Celestis' plan to replace current hybrid search stack (BM25 + in-house FAISS) with a managed embeddings + rerank flow. Key concerns: throughput (1k qps goal for retrieval+rerank), index dimensionality and cost (1536 vs 768 dims), vector DB choice, private deployment / VPC networking, and latency SLOs for p95/p99. Next: Redwood to share pricing + benchmarks; customer to provide dataset for pilot.

00:00 Alex Morgan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, um this is Alex from Redwood. I think we have like 40 minutes, we'll do some discovery, figure out constraints then Priya will do some technical Qs, ok?
00:12 Dana Lee: Awesome, thanks Alex. I'm Dana, I run search at Celestis. Quick intro — we do clinical docs search, mix of long medical notes and shorter summaries. Latency is important for clinician workflow.
00:25 Marco Ruiz: Marco here. We currently run BM25 + a FAISS reranker service that uses 1536-d embeddings, it's... it's okay but costs are spiking and ops is heavy.
00:36 Priya Shah: Hi Marco, thanks — can you clarify current QPS and latency targets?
00:41 Marco Ruiz: Sure, avg 250 qps today, peak around 700 during morning syncs; our target for product is 1k qps steady with p95 < 200ms end-to-end for retrieval + rerank if possible.
00:56 Emily Chen: From infra side, we prefer VPC peering and want to avoid exporting PHI out of our VPC; SOC2 and audit logs are must-haves.
01:08 Alex Morgan: Great, good constraints to know. Quick question: are you open to Hosted initially or do you need Dedicated/Private from day one because of PHI?
01:17 Dana Lee: We're evaluating options. Security team prefers Private, but business wants speed. We might start Hosted in a controlled way with DLP and then move to Dedicated or Private for full PHI workloads.
01:31 Priya Shah: Ok makes sense. On the embedding side — are you generating embeddings in-house or using a managed provider? Also what dimension are you using?
01:41 Marco Ruiz: We're currently producing 1536-d from an open model, doing a dense dot-product ann index in FAISS, then a small transformer reranker for top-50.
01:51 Priya Shah: Got it. A few of the things we typically dig into: index type (HNSW vs IVF + PQ), dimensionality tradeoffs (1536 vs 768), whether you need exact hybrid scoring (BM25+embed combining), and throughput/cost targets.
02:05 Marco Ruiz: The hybrid score is important — clinicians rely on term matches plus semantic. We currently combine BM25 score with dot product. Curious how Redwood handles hybrid setups and rerank latency.
02:16 Alex Morgan: Redwood supports hybrid search patterns several ways: you can do a BM25 pass in your DB and then call Redwood for dense rerank, or host an integrated flow where we return dense nearest neighbors and score client-side. For Dedicated/Private we can deploy a tight VPC-connected cluster that keeps embeddings and indexes inside your network, and we support streaming rerank so you can avoid large payloads.
02:38 Dana Lee: Can you support vector DBs like Pinecone or Qdrant or do we need to re-index inside Redwood?
02:45 Priya Shah: We can integrate with external vector DBs — typical patterns: 1) keep index in your DB (Pinecone/Qdrant/Milvus) and call Redwood for embed generation + rerank; 2) ingest embeddings into Redwood Dedicated index for co-located retrieval + rerank which reduces network hops. Both are supported; tradeoffs are latency vs control.
03:05 Marco Ruiz: If we keep index in Pinecone, what's the extra latency of rerank? We need p95 <200ms.
03:11 Priya Shah: It depends on network distance and batch sizes. For Hosted flow: embed gen + Pinecone lookup + rerank call back to Redwood can add 60-150ms network depending on region and concurrency. If you colocate (Dedicated) we often see retrieval + rerank p95s in 80-140ms at 500-1k qps for optimized models. But we'll benchmark with your dataset to calibrate.
03:34 Emily Chen: We need VPC peering for Dedicated; how does keystore/KMS integration work?
03:40 Alex Morgan: We support customer KMS (AWS KMS/HSM) in Private and Dedicated. For VPC we do peering or private link; all audit logs and request traces can be forwarded to your SIEM. We'll include SOC2 and pen-test reports.
03:53 Dana Lee: About dimensionality — do you recommend 1536 or 768? Our reranker expects 1536 inputs.
04:00 Priya Shah: Short answer: 1536 tends to give better semantic granularity but costs more (storage + ANN performance). 768 can be a sweet spot if you retrain/finetune or quantize. We also recommend experiments: run A/B on 768 vs 1536, try PQ/OPQ for IVF/PQ to reduce index size, and consider model distillation for lower dims. Redwood Optimize has suggestions for quant profiles.
04:22 Marco Ruiz: We also use batching for embed gen — what batching do you recommend for 1k qps?
04:28 Priya Shah: For 1k qps, continuous batching and micro-batching at the runtime layer helps. On Dedicated, you can set batching windows to hit GPU utilization targets; we provide per-route throughput controls and autoscale. Example: target latency 100-200ms, you might batch 8-16 requests for generation embeddings depending on sequence length. We'll share typical config.
04:49 Dana Lee: How do you support rerank models — can we upload our own reranker or do we use Redwood hosted model?
04:55 Priya Shah: Both. You can bring your own model artifact (container or model weights) for Private/Dedicated, or use Redwood-hosted reranker models. For hosted we limit custom models for security; but for Dedicated/Private we can run customer models behind your VPC.
05:09 Marco Ruiz: For the rerank step we currently do top-50 kNN and then rerank; any guidance on efficient hybrid rerank?
05:15 Priya Shah: Typical pattern: retrieve top-k dense hits (k 50-200), merge with BM25 candidates, dedupe, then run reranker on combined set. For cost we recommend upper-bounding the reranker to top-100 and use a lightweight cross-encoder when possible. You'll see better latency if reranker is optimized and quantized.
05:33 Alex Morgan: Another operational point — how do you manage embeddings lifecycle, reindexing and versioning?
05:37 Dana Lee: We reindex monthly for new clinical taxonomies; re-embedding takes hours and we need a zero-downtime switch.
05:44 Priya Shah: Redwood supports model/version tagging and rolling rollouts for index swaps. We can do blue/green reindexes with aliasing to avoid downtime. For large corpora we also support incremental updates.
05:58 Marco Ruiz: What about approximate recall — we need recall > 0.92 at top-50. How do you validate?
06:04 Priya Shah: We run offline evals against labeled query sets (mrr, recall@k, nDCG). Redwood's eval harness can run side-by-side A/Bs and trigger regression alerts if quality drops. We'll want your labelled dev set for this.
06:18 Emily Chen: Anything else on compliance? We need retention windows configurable and full audit trail per request.
06:25 Alex Morgan: Yep — configurable retention, granular audit logs, RBAC/SAML SSO and exportable logs for compliance.
06:31 Dana Lee: Who else at Redwood would we work with for a pilot?
06:36 Alex Morgan: On my side Priya will lead technical setup, SE-run benchmarks, and I will handle pricing/contract. Should we target a two-week pilot to validate latency and recall?
06:45 Marco Ruiz: That sounds good. We'll provide a 10k doc sample + 500 query val set and baseline metrics.
06:51 Priya Shah: Perfect — we'll run two pilot modes: 1) Hosted + external vector DB (your Pinecone) to prove quality quickly, 2) Dedicated co-located index to prove latency and cost. We'll compare and recommend.
07:05 Dana Lee: One more — can Redwood do hybrid search where BM25 + ANN are combined in one endpoint?
07:10 Priya Shah: We can orchestrate hybrid flows either client-side or server-side. For Dedicated we can do in-service hybrid ranking so only one call is needed. For Hosted we often recommend client orchestrate BM25 then call Redwood for rerank if you already have BM25 in your stack.
07:24 Marco Ruiz: Any rough cost numbers for index storage and p50 token cost?
07:29 Alex Morgan: We'll send pricing with ranges — rough thumb: co-located Dedicated index will reduce per-query network egress costs but has base infra commit. Hosted is lowest friction but higher per-op unit costs. We'll include ballpark storage $/GB and qps-tiered pricing in the follow-up.
07:43 Emily Chen: Ok — last logistics question: can we run a short performance test on our data in your sandbox? we need to keep PHI inside VPC though.
07:51 Priya Shah: For PHI we recommend Dedicated or Private pilot. We can set up a VPC peering sandbox or provide an on-prem package if needed. We'll provide instructions for sample upload and benchmark harness.
08:04 Alex Morgan: Great. I'll capture next steps. Dana, Marco, Emily — any other questions?
08:09 Dana Lee: No, sounds good. We'll aim to have the sample dataset ready in a few days.
08:13 Marco Ruiz: Thanks, appreciate the clarity.
08:15 Alex Morgan: Thanks everyone. Priya and I will follow up with docs, pricing, and schedule the deep dive.
